title: Best Rowing Machines UK
short: Home rowing machines compared by resistance type, connectivity and comfort, from budget-friendly to premium smart rowers.
intro: A rowing machine gives a genuinely zero-impact, full-body cardio workout, but comfort, noise and screen quality vary hugely between models. This guide compares rowers tested by Men's Fitness in their own homes for at least a month each, covering the full damper range, connectivity and storage.

products.name: RW900 Rower
products.best_for: Buyers with the space and budget for a premium, feature-packed rower
products.key_spec: 22in touchscreen, SmartAdjust machine learning, 10-year frame warranty
products.summary: Men's Fitness's top pick, smooth and ultra-quiet running similar to machines seen in commercial gyms, with a large tilting touchscreen and SmartAdjust technology that tailors every workout to your progress. It's a genuine investment with an ongoing membership fee, plus a large, bulky footprint that needs real space to store.

products.name: Strong Series Rower
products.best_for: Buyers who get bored easily and want entertainment built in
products.key_spec: 22in touchscreen, dual air/magnetic resistance, streaming service access included
products.summary: Men's Fitness found the dual air and magnetic resistance gives an authentic rowing feel with plenty of fine-tuning, and a Whisper nylon belt kept noise genuinely low. Membership unlocks not just guided workouts but Netflix, Disney+ and Spotify too, which testers found kept sessions properly entertaining, though it needs tall ceilings and a fair amount of space.

products.name: Original Series
products.badge: Best for indoor storage and authentic feel
products.best_for: Buyers who want the most realistic rowing motion and a striking design
products.key_spec: Water flywheel resistance, S4 Performance Monitor, wood finish
products.summary: Uses a water flywheel for what Men's Fitness called a smooth, realistic and immersive rowing experience unlike any other machine tested, with a striking wooden design that suits smart home interiors. The standard monitor is fairly basic, though Bluetooth and third-party app upgrades are available, and it's comparatively compact for storage.
cons: Low seat and steep angled foot position
High price once you add extras

products.name: Wave Rower
products.best_for: Buyers who want Hydrow's connected experience in a smaller footprint
products.key_spec: 16in touchscreen, compact brushed aluminium design, custom colourways
products.summary: Smaller and cheaper than the original Hydrow, with a sleek, minimal design Men's Fitness found genuinely space-saving alongside smooth, quiet operation. It gives access to engaging live and on-demand classes for a connected fitness experience, though the screen can be tricky to operate and Bluetooth audio has a noticeable delay.
cons: Screen can be tricky to operate

guide.q: Air, magnetic or water resistance: what's the difference?
guide.a: Air resistance rowers get harder to pull the faster you row, giving a natural, athletic feel favoured by serious rowers. Magnetic resistance is quieter and more consistent, good for shared living spaces. Water resistance, like the WaterRower here, aims to replicate the actual feel and sound of rowing on open water.

guide.q: Do I need a smart, subscription-based rower?
guide.a: A smart rower with a large touchscreen and guided classes, like the NordicTrack or Aviron here, genuinely helps with motivation and structure, but comes with an ongoing monthly membership cost on top of the purchase price. A simpler rower with a basic monitor, like the standard WaterRower, covers the core workout without recurring fees.

guide.q: How much space do I actually need?
guide.a: Plan for roughly 2.4m x 0.6m (8ft x 2ft) of clear floor space while rowing, plus extra height clearance for taller machines like the Aviron. Many rowers fold or stand upright for storage, like the Aviron and WaterRower here, which matters if you don't have a dedicated home gym space.

guide.q: What are the actual fitness benefits over other cardio machines?
guide.a: Rowing is zero-impact, unlike running, and works nearly every major muscle group across the drive phase: legs, then core, then upper body. Men's Fitness notes it also achieves higher oxygen consumption at a lower heart rate than treadmill workouts, while still burning a serious number of calories.
